question: Which of the following caves contain rock cut paintings dating back to the stone age era?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhimbetka Caves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhimbetka Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• The rock shelters of Bhimbetka contain paintings that date back to the Stone Age, specifically the Mesolithic period (c. 10,000 BCE).
 
• These paintings depict scenes from everyday life, including hunting, dancing, and communal activities, providing insights into the lives of early humans.
 
• The art includes representations of animals such as bison, tigers, and elephants, as well as human figures engaged in activities.
 
• The Bhimbetka Cave complex is one of the earliest examples of human interaction with the environment, showcasing continuity in artistic expression over thousands of years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rock Art Terminology:**

 
 
• Rock art refers to human-made markings placed on natural stone, typically in caves or open-air shelters.
 
• It includes petroglyphs (carvings) and pictographs (paintings).
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**
 
 
• Bhimbetka was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003 due to its archaeological and cultural significance.
 
• The site is noted for its unique record of human settlement and evolution over different historical periods.
 
 
 
• **Mesolithic Period:**
 
 
• The Mesolithic period, also known as the Middle Stone Age, is characterized by the transition from hunting and gathering to agriculture.
 
• Rock art from this period is significant for its depiction of social and cultural development.
 
 
 
• **Discovery of Bhimbetka:**
 
 
• The caves were first discovered by Indian archaeologist V.S. Wakankar in 1957 while surveying the Narmada Valley.
 
• Over 750 rock shelters have been identified, with around 500 containing paintings.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Sites:**
 
 
• Other significant rock art sites in India include the Adamgarh Hills (Madhya Pradesh) and the Kupgal petroglyphs (Karnataka).
 
• Globally, comparable sites include the Lascaux Caves in France and the Altamira Cave in Spain.
